assets.identity_finding: Kraken publishes the asset as Adi Token on Ethereum (ERC-20). Independently, the ADI Foundation's own blog post introducing the ADI token publishes the literal line Official Contract Address (ERC-20): 0x8b1484d57abbe239bb280661377363b03c89caea and states that $ADI launches as an ERC-20 token on Ethereum at TGE, and the foundation's own documentation at docs.adi.foundation sets out the same token's utility. Both organisations agree on ticker, chain and token standard, and the record binds the published contract.

Kraken publishes the asset as Avantis on Base. Independently, the project's own documentation on its avantisfi.com domain publishes the $AVNT Contract Address 0x696F9436B67233384889472Cd7cD58A6fB5DF4f1 together with Token Ticker $AVNT, Type ERC20, Chain Base and Total Supply (Fixed) 1,000,000,000. Both organisations agree on ticker, chain and token standard, and the record binds the published contract. REBRAND DISCLOSURE: the project's documentation is now titled Veranta and describes $AVNT as the connective tissue of the Veranta ecosystem, while Kraken still publishes the name Avantis; the docs remain on the project's original avantisfi.com domain, so this is one project under a new brand rather than a ticker collision, and the binding identifier is the contract address rather than the brand name.

Kraken publishes the asset as Axie Infinity Shards on Ethereum (ERC-20). Independently, Axie Infinity's own whitepaper states that the $AXS and $SLP ERC-20 contract has been audited by Quantstamp and links the audit report, and the project's own key-smart-contracts page enumerates its Ethereum contracts. Both organisations therefore agree on ticker, chain and token standard. DISCLOSED LIMIT: none of the officially reachable Axie Infinity pages publishes the AXS contract address as text -- only third-party explorers do, and those were not accepted -- so this record is a chain-level identity confirmed by two independent organisations and makes no exact-contract claim.

Kraken publishes the asset as MultiversX on the Elrond network, the project's own chain under its former name. Independently, MultiversX's own integrators documentation is titled and written as the integration guide for MultiversX's native coin, EGLD, and the project's own EGLD page states that EGLD is MultiversX's native asset for security, gas fees and governance and that ESDT is the MultiversX native token standard distinct from EGLD itself. Both organisations agree on ticker, chain and project. This is a native-coin identity on the project's own layer-1, the same source shape as the ratified ETC and VET native-coin records, so there is no contract address to bind and none is claimed.

Kraken publishes the asset as Grass on Solana. Independently, the Grass project's own site states that the Grass wallet is running on Solana, and the Grass Foundation's own GRASS Tokenomics documentation publishes the GRASS token supply, allocation and monthly distribution schedule. Both organisations therefore agree on ticker and chain. DISCLOSED LIMIT: no officially reachable Grass page publishes the SPL mint address -- the widely cited mint appears only on third-party explorers and aggregators, which were not accepted -- so this record is a chain-level identity confirmed by two independent organisations and makes no exact-contract claim.

Kraken publishes the asset as MegaETH on the MegaETH network, the project's own chain. Independently, MegaETH's own developer documentation publishes a Contracts and Tokens table for MegaETH mainnet listing MEGA at 0x28B7E77f82B25B95953825F1E3eA0E36c1c29861 with the description MegaETH's native protocol token, sourced from the project's own mega-tokenlist registry. Both organisations agree on ticker, chain and project, and the record binds the published contract.

Kraken publishes the asset as Moonriver on Base, which on its face looked like a catalog quirk because Moonriver was the native coin of a Kusama parachain. Independently, the Moonbeam Foundation's own announcement, republished verbatim from moonbeam.network, states that it is announcing the full migration of the MOVR token to Base, that the migration is 1:1 so every MOVR becomes one Base ERC-20 MOVR, that holders must bridge before 2026-07-31, and that the new MOVR token on Base is deployed to the new address 0x43fEB74608334DDa8c1a6500D185cFC3Ea962B83; the foundation's own Moonriver tokenomics page covers the same token. Both organisations therefore agree on ticker and chain, and the apparent discrepancy is resolved: Kraken's Base designation reflects a real, project-executed migration. The record binds the published Base contract.

Kraken publishes the asset as OKB on XLayer. Independently, OKX's own X Layer site states that OKB is X Layer's native gas token, the key to the blockchain's operations and governance, its own X Layer developer documentation records the gas token as OKB with a fixed supply at 21M post-burns/upgrades and the L1 OKB phased out, and its own help-centre article documents OKB as the native gas token for X Layer alongside the OKT consolidation. Both organisations agree on ticker and chain, and OKX's publication independently explains why Kraken's network is XLayer rather than Ethereum: the former ERC-20 representation has been retired in favour of the native X Layer gas coin. This is a native gas-coin identity, so there is no contract address to bind and none is claimed. CAPTURE NOTE: okx.com returns an empty body to a headless-Chrome render, so these three OKX bodies were retained over a plain HTTP request with a browser user agent.

Kraken publishes the asset as Ponke on Solana. Independently, the project's own site at ponke.xyz publishes the token's Solana mint 5z3EqYQo9HiCEs3R84RCDMu2n7anpDMxRhdK8PSWmrRC and states that Ponke is multichain with SOLANA as the original chain and BASE as the expansion chain. Both organisations agree on ticker and chain, and the record binds the published Solana mint, which is the representation Kraken lists.

Kraken publishes the asset as Robo Token on Ethereum (ERC-20). Independently, the Fabric Foundation -- a non-profit advancing open robotics and AGI, per its own site -- publishes a whitepaper stating that $ROBO is a utility token used exclusively to pay on-network fees and to post operational bonds, that it initially launched as an ERC20 token on Ethereum mainnet to support a phased rollout, and that the protocol's functionality is deployed through smart contracts on EVM-compatible chains such as Ethereum Mainnet and Coinbase's Base L2. Both organisations therefore agree on ticker, chain and token standard. DISCLOSED LIMIT: no official page publishes a contract address, so this record is a chain-level identity confirmed by two independent organisations and makes no exact-contract claim.

Kraken publishes the asset as Turbo on Ethereum (ERC-20). The only candidate second source is turbotoken.io, which does publish the contract address 0xa35923162c49cf95e6bf26623385eb431ad920d3 and describes TURBO as a community-driven, fully decentralised token coded by artificial intelligence -- but that same page states verbatim that "This website is an independent, community-driven platform and does NOT officially represent TURBO" and that "The TURBO community operates as a decentralized entity and is not responsible for how individuals or organizations choose to use TURBO". RULING: a page that explicitly declines to represent the asset cannot be the second independent source the ratified bar requires, however accurate its contract string may be. That TURBO has no issuer is a real fact about TURBO, and the honest way to record a token whose identity nobody authoritative publishes is to say it could not be confirmed, rather than to accept the nearest available page because nothing better exists. Kraken's own metadata carries no chain, contract or genesis field, so nothing remains to match independently. This is the PLAY / RE / MOODENG case: a ratified exclusion from the source-coverage universe, not a judgement that the asset is unsuitable for investment. The evidence above is retained in full precisely so a future reader can overturn this record if a genuine issuer source appears.

Kraken publishes the asset as VeThor on VeChain. Independently, VeChain's own documentation describes the dual-token economic model and publishes VTHO's built-in contract address 0x0000000000000000000000000000456E65726779 with the VIP180 token standard, and its built-in-contracts reference lists the same Energy contract. Both organisations agree on ticker, chain and token standard, and the record binds the published contract. The record is explicitly distinct from VET, the other token of the same VeChain dual-token network, which already carries its own ratified record.

Kraken publishes the asset as Zerebro on Solana and its own asset page describes Zerebro as a decentralised platform combining AI and blockchain whose native token is on Solana -- but that is one organisation, and Kraken's own Assets/AssetPairs metadata carries no chain, contract or genesis field. No second, project-controlled publication could be obtained to match it independently: the project's own domain zerebro.org returns a Next.js page whose entire body is a single animated canvas element with no token, chain, mint or contract text anywhere in the retained DOM; the research paper path cited for the project returns HTTP 404; and the ZerePy repository under the Blorm organisation documents an open-source agent framework built from the Zerebro backend without publishing any token identity. Every SPL mint claim for this ticker traces to third-party explorers, exchanges and aggregators, which the ratified bar does not accept. This is the PLAY / RE / MOODENG case: a genuine, evidenced identity failure recorded as a ratified exclusion, not a judgement that the asset is unsuitable for investment.

scope: Source-coverage universe identity only: not investability, not capacity, not venue selection, not candidate promotion, not Regime activation, not Production wiring, not trading authority.
verification_bar: Two independent official sources per asset: the retained Kraken catalog (enabled asset with exactly one online <ASSET>/USD pair) plus Kraken's published asset name and network, matched independently against a project/foundation protocol document, token contract publication, migration notice or exact-contract asset report. Ticker text alone was not accepted. Kraken's own metadata carries no chain, contract or genesis field, so Kraken alone never satisfies the bar. Where the project publishes an exact contract or mint the record binds that identifier; where it publishes only the chain and token standard the record says so explicitly and claims no contract. Where two independent official sources could not be obtained, the asset is recorded as unverified_identity with its evidence, or left unclassified where there is no evidence either way.
